content: Tins::IP.ttl field is a Time-To-Live field in the IP header of a packet. It specifies the maximum number of hops (routers) the packet can take before being discarded. As the packet passes through each router, the TTL value is decremented by one. If the TTL reaches zero, the packet is discarded and an ICMP error message is sent back to the sender. This field is used to prevent packets from circulating endlessly in a network.
